{{Short description|Of a Kronecker product (combinatorics)}}
In mathematics, '''Kronecker coefficients''' ''g''{{su|p=λ|b=''μν''}} describe the decomposition of the [[tensor product]] (=&nbsp;[[Kronecker product]]) of two [[irreducible representation]]s of a [[symmetric group]] into irreducible representations. They play an important role in [[algebraic combinatorics]] and [[geometric complexity theory]]. They were introduced by [[Francis Dominic Murnaghan (mathematician)|Murnaghan]] in 1938.

== Definition == 
Given a partition λ of ''n'', write ''V''<sub>λ</sub> for the [[Specht module]] associated to λ. Then the Kronecker coefficients ''g''<sup>λ</sup><sub>''μν''</sub> are given by the rule

:<math> V_\mu \otimes V_\nu = \bigoplus_\lambda g_{\mu \nu}^{\lambda} V_\lambda.  </math>

One can interpret this on the level of [[symmetric function]]s, giving a formula for the Kronecker product of two [[Schur polynomial]]s:

:<math>s_\mu \star s_\nu = \sum_{\lambda} g_{\mu \nu}^{\lambda} s_\lambda.</math>

This is to be compared with [[Littlewood–Richardson coefficient]]s, where one instead considers the induced representation

:<math> \uparrow_{S_{|\mu|} \times S_{|\nu|}}^{S_{|\lambda|}} \left ( V_\mu \otimes V_\nu \right ) = \bigoplus_\lambda c_{\mu \nu}^{\lambda} V_\lambda,  </math>

and the corresponding operation of symmetric functions is the usual product. Also note that the Littlewood–Richardson coefficients are the analogue of the Kronecker coefficients for representations of GL<sub>''n''</sub>, i.e. if we write ''W''<sub>λ</sub> for the irreducible representation corresponding to λ (where λ has at most ''n'' parts), one gets that

:<math> W_\mu \otimes W_\nu = \bigoplus_\lambda c_{\mu \nu}^{\lambda} W_\lambda.  </math>

== Properties ==

{{harvtxt|Bürgisser|Ikenmeyer|2008}} showed that computing Kronecker coefficients is [[♯P|#P-hard]] and contained in [[GapP]]. A later work by {{harvtxt|Ikenmeyer|Mulmuley|Walter|2017}} shows that deciding whether a given Kronecker coefficient is non-zero is [[NP-hardness|NP-hard]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ikenmeyer|first1=Christian|last2=Mulmuley|first2=Ketan D.|last3=Walter|first3=Michael|date=2017-12-01|title=On vanishing of Kronecker coefficients|journal=Computational Complexity|language=en|volume=26|issue=4|pages=949–992|doi=10.1007/s00037-017-0158-y|issn=1420-8954|arxiv=1507.02955|s2cid=1126187}}</ref> This interest in computational complexity of these coefficients arises from its relevance in the [[Geometric complexity theory|Geometric Complexity Theory]] program. 

A major unsolved problem in representation theory and combinatorics is to give a combinatorial description of the Kronecker coefficients. It has been open since 1938, when [[Francis Dominic Murnaghan (mathematician)|Murnaghan]] asked for such a combinatorial description.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Murnaghan|first1=D.|title=The Analysis of the Direct Product of Irreducible Representations of the Symmetric Groups|journal=Amer. J. Math.|date=1938|volume=60|issue=9|pages=44–65|doi=10.2307/2371542|pmid=16577800|pmc=1076971|jstor=2371542}}</ref> A combinatorial description would also imply that the problem is [[♯P-complete|#P-complete]] in light of the above result.

The Kronecker coefficients can be computed as
<math display="block"> g(\lambda, \mu, \nu) = \frac{1}{n!} \sum_{\sigma \in S_n} \chi^{\lambda}(\sigma)\chi^{\mu}(\sigma)\chi^{\nu}(\sigma), </math>
where <math>\chi^{\lambda}(\sigma)</math> is the [[Character theory|character value]] of the irreducible representation corresponding to [[integer partition]] <math>\lambda</math> on a permutation <math>\sigma \in S_n</math>.

The Kronecker coefficients also appear in the generalized Cauchy identity
<math display="block"> \sum_{\lambda, \mu, \nu} g(\lambda, \mu , \nu) s_\lambda(x)s_\mu(y)s_\nu(z) = \prod_{i,j,k} \frac{1}{1-x_iy_jz_k}. </math>
